name: Demo shop
description: A small tea & coffee shop: products, customers, orders, a view, a materialized view, a linked CSV of exchange rates and sales data imported from a Parquet file. Sample data only.

queries.title: Revenue by category
queries.sql:
-- Ctrl+Enter runs the statement under the cursor
SELECT category,
       count(*) AS lines,
       sum(quantity) AS units,
       round(sum(amount), 2) AS revenue
FROM order_lines
WHERE status <> 'cancelled'
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY revenue DESC;

-- Top customers, revenue converted to USD through the linked exchange_rates CSV
SELECT c.name, c.country, c.currency,
       round(sum(o.quantity * p.price), 2) AS revenue,
       round(sum(o.quantity * p.price) * r.usd_per_unit, 2) AS revenue_usd
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id
JOIN exchange_rates r ON r.currency = c.currency
GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.country, c.currency, r.usd_per_unit
ORDER BY revenue_usd DESC
LIMIT 10;

queries.title: Window functions
Parquet
queries.sql:
-- regional_sales was imported from a Parquet file (data/regional_sales.parquet).
-- The Import tab and environment "import" steps read Parquet like CSV or JSON.
SELECT region,
       count(*) AS sales,
       sum(amount) AS total,
       min(day) AS first_day,
       max(day) AS last_day
FROM regional_sales
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY total DESC;

-- Monthly totals per region
SELECT substr(day, 1, 7) AS month, region, sum(amount) AS total
FROM regional_sales
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC
LIMIT 24;

cells.source:
-- A SQL cell runs in smaltql. Its result is _1: a smaltdf LazyFrame over this query.
SELECT category, product, quantity, amount, status
FROM order_lines
WHERE status <> 'cancelled';

// A dataframe cell runs smaltdf: the Polars expression API, compiled to SQL and run by smaltdb.
_1.groupBy('category')
  .agg(col('amount').sum().round(2).alias('revenue'), len().alias('lines'))
  .sort('revenue', { descending: true })

-- Back to SQL: the monthly revenue materialized view.
SELECT month, orders, revenue FROM monthly_revenue ORDER BY month;

// explain() shows the single SQL statement a frame runs.
await _3.explain()
